title: Schedule PI control across a gravity tank's operating range
physicalPurpose: Hold liquid level consistently while gravity outflow changes plant dynamics across the operating range.
principalTechnique: Validated local models with atomic interpolation or hysteretically selected tracked PIs
objective: Derive and validate local models of a gravity-drained tank, then decide whether one fixed proportional-integral controller or either of two gain-scheduling architectures gives consistent control over the full operating range without creating output bumps or boundary chatter.

simplifications: One well-mixed vertical tank with constant area and a fixed gravity outlet
Ideal pump flow equals the bounded controller request; pump dynamics are deferred
Local first-order models are valid only near their identified equilibrium levels
Three equivalent simulated tanks isolate controller architecture
Simulation-only I/O and evidence; no physical tank is operated

baseline.limitation: The conservative high-level integral gain is unnecessarily slow in the low-level region.

change.decision: Accept scheduling only when every local model is qualified, constraints remain common, regional performance improves, and both transition architectures are bumpless.

disturbances: Use separate restored boundary holds to test sensor-noise chatter

acceptance.window: worst of four commanded regions from 30 through 420 s
worst of four commanded regions from 30 through 420 s
adjacent samples at each region transition

abortPredicates: Any required signal is nonfinite, stale, forced, or invalid
A tank level leaves 0.20 through 0.90 m
A pump request leaves 0 through 0.060 m3/s
The schedule is invalid or clamped during an accepted run
Parallel selection chatters or exceeds the transition count
An inactive controller does not track selected pump flow
safety.restorationMode: Remove scheduling authority, track every controller to zero pump flow, restore the simulated tank, then requalify models and scheduling data.
safety.physicalApprovalRole: authorised process-control engineer and responsible tank-system owner
simulationOnlyRestrictions: No physical pump or tank is operated
Simulation model truth is not identified-model or physical-plant evidence
Physical commissioning requires reviewed topology, protections, limits, restoration and explicit approval

video.viewerOutcome: Derive local gravity-tank models, configure two scheduling architectures, and validate regional performance and transitions.

learning.context: Three equivalent vented tanks receive bounded inlet-pump flow and drain through a square-root gravity outlet.
learning.reason: Unlike Lesson 57's priority change, control authority remains level regulation while plant gain and time constant change with level.
theory: Mass conservation and square-root outflow produce operating-point-dependent local first-order dynamics.
A validated requested operating level schedules one atomic parameter record for a retained PI state.
Parallel local PIs require hysteresis and external tracking.
learning.workedPrediction: At 0.30, 0.55 and 0.80 m, equilibrium flows are 0.02739, 0.03708 and 0.04472 m3/s and local time constants are 21.91, 29.66 and 35.78 s.
practicalPreparation: Verify Simulation evidence, identities, SI units, model envelope, validity, quality, timing, limits and restoration.
Define regional IAE, settling, pump travel, transition count and transition-step validity before results.
learning.baseline: Run the conservative high-level PI through the complete low-middle-high-middle-low sequence.
learning.change: Use either atomically interpolated local parameters in one PI or hysteretically select three externally tracked local PIs.
learning.comparison: Hold nonlinear equations, initial state, requests, constraints, timing, seed and windows equal while changing only controller architecture.
learning.validation: Require bounded signals, better worst-region IAE than fixed PI, exactly four parallel transitions, no chatter and no transition step above 0.0005 m3/s.
learning.explanation: Square-root outflow changes local dynamics; scheduling matches integral action while atomic updates or tracking preserve continuity.
learning.transfer: Schedule only from validated operating dependence; Lesson 59 addresses long transport delay.
